# Calls that quote your account number

Firthmoor Bank's careless handling of its customers' data has left names, addresses and mortgage account numbers exposed, the Clyde Money Review reports. The bank said no passwords or card details were taken and that it had written to everyone affected.

Criminals can use stolen details like these to sound convincing on the phone. A caller who knows your account number has not proved that the call is genuine.

If you get a call or text about your mortgage that you were not expecting, end it and contact your lender using the number on your statement. A genuine lender will not mind you checking, and will never ask you to move money to keep it safe. If a call feels wrong, it is fine to hang up.
